title: Stop, stabilize, signal

action.text: Pause on stable ground and check the scene before approaching an injured person. Check responsiveness, breathing and obvious life-threatening injury.
If someone is unresponsive, breathing abnormally or bleeding severely, call 911 and follow the dispatcher. Give your location and the immediate hazard.
If travel has stopped, use available shelter and insulation. Tell everyone where to wait and who is trying to make contact.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Decide what needs action before the group moves.
applies: A walking party in Minnesota or the Upper Midwest with an unexpected delay, injury or loss of route.
equipment: Use a phone, communicator, whistle, headlamp and insulation if available.

verify.text: Each person can name the immediate hazard, the group's location or last known point, and who is attempting contact.

stop.text: Leave immediate danger by a clearly safer path. If location and safe travel are uncertain, stay findable and seek help.

diagram: Stop on safe ground | Check people and hazards | Signal and protect the group
visual: Role and decision sequence. Reading order follows the first actions.
reviewer: Wilderness medicine and search and rescue

title: Assess before you move

action.text: Inventory the group, the weather, the remaining daylight and the last place you can identify confidently.
Compare what you see with a mapped trail, junction or other reliable feature. Record the last verified place if your current location is uncertain.
Move only when the group can name a safe next checkpoint and is able to reach it. Keep current conditions and the slowest member in the decision.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Use location, daylight and group condition to decide whether travel makes sense.
applies: A stopped group with a potentially safe route and enough time to assess.
equipment: Offline map or paper map, watch, light and weather information if available.

verify.text: Before stepping off, someone can point to the next checkpoint and explain how the party will know it has reached it.

stop.text: Weather, terrain or group condition can invalidate a previously reasonable route. Halt if the next checkpoint becomes uncertain.

diagram: Last verified place | Check group and conditions | Name a safe next point
visual: Route-confidence decision schematic with three checkpoints.

title: Stay, signal or move

action.text: Stop. If an immediate hazard threatens the spot, reach safer ground nearby only when you can identify a safe way there.
Contact 911 when help is needed and service is available. Report last known position, landmarks, number of people, injuries and any planned movement.
If you cannot determine a safe route, stay together in a findable location, shelter from weather and prepare to signal when responders are nearby.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Make an explicit choice between staying findable and moving to a known safe position.
applies: Lost or overdue outdoor party. Immediate danger and known route are separate questions.
equipment: Phone or emergency communicator, whistle, light, bright material and weather protection if available.

verify.text: Your location description gives responders a usable starting point. Mark a plan change in your message if you must move.

stop.text: Never attempt an uncertain shortcut over water or ice to reach a signal or a road.

diagram: Immediate danger? | Safe route known? | If uncertain, stay findable
visual: Two-question decision sequence with a stay-put outcome.

title: Reject unsafe shelter sites

action.text: Check land rules and choose an established or designated site when required. Inspect the site and access route before unpacking.
Leave stream channels, low ground that can flood and other routes concentrating runoff. Upstream rain can reach a site even when the local sky is clear.
Scan overhead and upslope. Leave any spot where loose limbs, loose material or an unstable slope threaten the group.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Rule out unsafe sites before judging comfort or convenience.
applies: Choosing temporary cover or a permitted campsite on land. Site rules and local hazards vary.
equipment: Map and weather information if available. Use daylight for inspection where possible.

verify.text: Identify an exit to safer ground and a place for the party away from overhead hazards and drainage paths.

stop.text: Reject a site if you cannot confirm a clear exit or if runoff, wind or falling material threatens it.

diagram: Runoff channel | Higher site | Exit to higher ground
visual: Site cross-section with blue drainage path and a separate higher site. Terrain is conceptual and unscaled.

title: Block wind before building a roof

action.text: Choose the sheltered side of an existing stable barrier. Check that you remain clear of runoff and falling material.
Keep the exit easy to reach. Put on dry layers and protect yourself from the ground while conditions allow.
Reassess as wind direction or drifting changes. Seek a safer shelter if the barrier no longer works.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Reduce exposure using an available barrier while keeping an escape route.
applies: Cold wind or blowing snow. Stable site already selected.
equipment: Existing wind barrier, insulating layers and optional shelter material made for outdoor use.

verify.text: Group members can move out without climbing over a barrier. Clothing and bedding are staying dry.

stop.text: Leave unstable cover or a blocked exit. Keep fuel-burning equipment outside enclosed shelters.

diagram: Wind | Stable barrier | Sheltered side and clear exit
visual: Side view showing windward exposure and leeward waiting position with an open exit.

title: Make a dry insulated bed

action.text: Select ground away from runoff and above standing water. Keep dry gear out of splash and wet snow.
Place dry insulation between body and ground. Add dry layers above and keep protection available for wind and precipitation.
Check for gaps under the body and wet material after settling. Replace wet insulation or move if the site is deteriorating.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Reduce heat loss through contact with cold ground.
applies: Short-term rest outdoors on a safe, dry site.
equipment: Camping pad or other dry insulating layer, dry clothing and weather cover if available.

verify.text: The body is separated from cold ground and the bedding stays dry where the person rests.

stop.text: If the person becomes confused, very drowsy or loses coordination after cold exposure, seek help promptly.

diagram: Body and dry cover | Insulation below | Cold ground
visual: Layered side view distinguishes underbody insulation from upper cover.

title: Decide whether to light a fire

action.text: Check current restrictions and site rules. Skip a fire if the rules prohibit it or the answer is uncertain.
Evaluate wind, nearby vegetation and overhead hazards. Have water available and an attendant who can stay until it is fully out.
Use non-fire warmth or lighting if conditions or equipment are inadequate. Keep camping fuel appliances out of tents and enclosed sleeping areas.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Decide whether outdoor fire is lawful, controllable and necessary.
applies: Outdoor campfire in Minnesota. Local jurisdiction, fire restrictions and current weather apply.
equipment: Established ring where required, water and a stirring tool.

verify.text: Confirm lawful use, controllable conditions, water ready and a named attendant before ignition.

stop.text: Wind gusts, missing water or combustibles in the exposure area stop the setup.

diagram: Permission | Site and weather | Water and attendant
visual: Fire decision checks before ignition. All three must be satisfied.
reviewer: Fire prevention and local land management

title: Select dry tinder and kindling

action.text: Prepare dry tinder and separate it from wet, moldy or frozen surface material. Keep the prepared materials dry while staging.
Stage dry small kindling and then larger pieces. Dry tinder starts the flame; progressively larger material carries it after the smaller material burns.
Check the fire site again before ignition. Keep accelerants away and stay with the fire until it is out.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Recognize the difference between material that catches and material that carries a small fire.
applies: An authorized and controllable outdoor campfire site. For lawful collection, follow site rules.
equipment: Dry tinder, dry small kindling, larger dry fuel and extinguishing water.

verify.text: Tinder, kindling and fuel are distinguished, dry and ready before a match is struck.

stop.text: If you lack dry materials or the site cannot be controlled, change to the no-fire plan.

diagram: Fine dry tinder | Small dry kindling | Larger fuel
visual: Conceptual relative size comparison. Three distinct groups and no prescribed dimensions.

title: Keep warm without fire

action.text: Move to an identifiable safe sheltered spot. Get out of wind and off the cold ground.
Put on available dry insulation. Keep wet outer gear from soaking your dry layers.
Communicate location and plans if delayed or in distress. Monitor group coordination and alertness.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Shift attention from ignition attempts to exposure control.
applies: Cold, wet or windy conditions when fire is unavailable, unsafe, or prohibited.
equipment: Dry clothing, ground insulation, emergency shelter, light and communications if available.

verify.text: The group has protection below and around the body and someone knows how help will be requested.

stop.text: Seek emergency help for confusion, slurred speech or reduced responsiveness after cold exposure.

diagram: Wind protection | Dry layers | Insulation below
visual: Heat-loss pathways and corresponding barriers.

title: Catch rain as raw water

action.text: Choose materials with known prior use. Avoid collecting from roof, gutter or other surfaces where chemicals, droppings or debris may enter the supply.
Catch water into the raw-water vessel and close or cover it. Keep its outlet and utensils apart from the drinking container.
Use a confirmed safe supply for drinking if available. For a chemically acceptable source, choose a dependable microbial treatment before drinking.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Collect rain while keeping raw water separate from finished drinking water.
applies: Rain collection where lawful. Prioritize a known safe supply and avoid contaminated surfaces.
equipment: Clean food-contact catchment and vessel if available. Separate, labelled potable container.

verify.text: The raw vessel and clean vessel can be identified without relying on water clarity.

stop.text: If you suspect fuel or toxic chemicals, reject the source. Boiling or ordinary disinfection cannot correct that hazard.

diagram: Catch surface | Raw vessel | Separate clean vessel
visual: Material flow with a break between raw water and clean storage. Treatment takes place before transfer.

title: Turn acceptable snow into treated water

action.text: Reject snow near spills or suspected chemical contamination. Melt snow in a safe vessel; melting alone does not disinfect it.
Let cloudy meltwater settle or clarify it through a clean cloth. Then bring acceptable water to a rolling boil for one minute, or three minutes above 6,500 feet.
Let it cool and store it covered in a cleaned, sanitized container. Keep raw snow and utensils away from the finished water.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Keep source assessment, melting, microbial treatment and storage distinct.
applies: Snow as a fallback source. Slow or unsafe access, chemical contamination and weak ice rule out collection.
equipment: Clean heat-safe vessel, safe outdoor heat source, and clean covered storage.

verify.text: Record or track the rolling boil and active timer, then close the clean container.

stop.text: Use another supply if you cannot rule out a suspected chemical hazard or safely use the vessel and heat source.

diagram: Assess and melt | Clarify then treat | Cool, cover and store
visual: Four operations shown in three grouped blocks, with treatment explicitly independent from melting.

title: When you cannot treat water

action.text: Check for carried safe water or an accessible official source before collecting untreated water. Keep route safety in the choice.
If a known method is available, check what it is designed to remove. Cloth straining and clear appearance do not address microbial risks.
If no dependable method exists, communicate your location and need. Avoid creating another emergency by travelling an unsafe route to find water.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Recognize when a water-treatment fallback is unavailable.
applies: Outdoor delay without a reliable heat source, safe vessel or validated product.
equipment: Known-safe carried water if available. Communication and shelter equipment as conditions allow.

verify.text: Name the supply and the treatment steps you can actually perform before treating a collected source as drinking water.

stop.text: Suspected toxic contamination requires an alternate source even if you can boil or disinfect.

diagram: Safe supply available? | Matched treatment available? | If neither, seek help
visual: Treatment-limit decision strip. It contains no improvised potability test.

title: Leave a usable trip plan
origin: B014 reconstruction R01 and B012 P02

action.text: Record the starting point, planned route and return time. Include names or party size and expected vehicle location if relevant.
Give the plan to a trusted contact and agree on the overdue reporting point and what information to pass to responders.
Carry a copy and notify the contact of significant changes when you can. Check back in at return.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Give a trusted person enough information to help responders if you are overdue.
applies: A trip outside dependable cell service, especially an unfamiliar trail.
equipment: Paper plan or saved message, mapped route, and contact information.

verify.text: Your contact can identify the trailhead and say when they should act.

stop.text: If nobody can act on an overdue report, reconsider the route and exposure before departing.

diagram: Route and group | Return and overdue time | Contact acknowledges plan
visual: A trip plan is a handoff; the contact and the party have separate roles.
reviewer: Search and rescue and land management

title: Pack by failure mode

action.text: Map darkness, navigation loss, exposure and delayed return to independent kit functions. Consider Sun protection and repair supplies as conditions warrant.
Check each function at home: a light turns on, the map works offline, the shelter can be set up, and spare insulation is dry.
Give shared gear an owner. Ensure the group can reach critical pieces without emptying all the packs.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Match kit functions to foreseeable failures and practice using them.
applies: Day and overnight travel. Terrain, temperature and time without help shape the kit.
equipment: Map, light, insulation, shelter, water, food, first aid and other route-appropriate essentials.

verify.text: Simulate one failure and retrieve the correct item without a signal or a search through loose gear.

stop.text: Narrow or postpone the trip if critical protection or navigation is absent.

diagram: Anticipate failure | Match a kit function | Demonstrate it works
visual: Equipment checks link each object to a failure the party is likely to face.
reviewer: Field education and search and rescue

title: Set a turnaround before departure

action.text: Identify a decision point and latest turnaround time. Build in daylight and delay margin for the slowest group member.
At each reliable checkpoint compare actual progress and conditions with the plan. Recalculate when the return route or pace changes.
Turn back early if visibility, access, group condition or the return margin deteriorates and the return route is known safe.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Preserve the time and energy needed to return.
applies: An out-and-back trip where conditions, group speed or daylight can change.
equipment: Watch, map and reliable forecast or local advisory.

verify.text: The group can name the trigger and the place where it will reassess.

stop.text: If the return route is no longer safe or known, use the stay/signal decision rather than a guessed shortcut.

diagram: Set return margin | Compare at checkpoints | Turn back while able
visual: A decision occurs before the intended destination when the return margin is lost.

title: Give rescuers a usable location

action.text: Give the site or park name plus trailhead, road, junction or other verified landmark. If sending coordinates, read the format shown by the device.
State how many people are involved, whether anyone is injured and what nearby hazards affect access.
Specify whether you will wait or must move. Follow dispatcher directions and communicate changes if you can.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Report what you know and identify uncertainty explicitly.
applies: Calling for rescue at an outdoor emergency in the United States.
equipment: Phone or suitable communicator, offline map and light if available.

verify.text: Ask whether your location was received and which approach the responder wants you to use, if any.

stop.text: Avoid moving solely to improve service if the route is uncertain or hazardous.

diagram: Give verified location | Describe people and hazards | Confirm follow-up
visual: Dispatch handoff sequence with known location separated from uncertain information.

title: Pitch a purpose-made shelter
origin: B012 P12 and B003 tarp plate

action.text: Pick a legal durable site outside runoff channels and clear of overhead hazards. Check the immediate weather before setting up.
Assemble the shelter according to its instructions. Keep exits and equipment access clear and avoid putting wet gear on dry bedding.
Inspect all attachment points and observe how the shelter responds to wind. Adjust within manufacturer limits or relocate to suitable shelter.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Use a known shelter system on a site that stays safe in changing conditions.
applies: A commercial tent or tarp in its intended weather range on a permitted site.
equipment: Shelter, parts and instructions for the exact model; dry pad and insulation.

verify.text: The shelter remains stable, rain drains away from the bed, and each occupant can exit without unfastening gear.

stop.text: If wind, runoff or structural movement exceeds what you can manage safely, leave for more suitable cover.

diagram: Safe durable site | Pitch per instructions | Inspect anchors and exits
visual: Three-step inspection card for design-specific shelter setup.

title: Leave a drainage channel early
origin: B012 P09 and agency flood guide

action.text: Look for connected low ground and a clear route to higher ground. Study upstream conditions as part of the decision.
Select a higher, stable site away from streambeds and gullies. Be ready to move if warnings, rising water or new runoff appear.
Leave early by a safe route to higher ground. Follow local emergency directions.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Recognize where moving water will concentrate before precipitation reaches the site.
applies: Campsites and travel near creeks, gullies, marsh edges and valley bottoms.
equipment: Map, weather alerts and a light if available.

verify.text: Someone in the group can identify both the hazard path and the exit without entering the drainage.

stop.text: Never cross flooded routes to retrieve gear or reach the planned exit.

diagram: Trace the drainage | Choose higher ground | Leave before routes flood
visual: An unscaled hazard sequence emphasizing early departure.

title: Seek lightning-safe shelter

action.text: Plan a way to reach a substantial building or enclosed hard-topped vehicle before storms develop.
At thunder, stop outdoor activity and get to the identified shelter if safely accessible. A fabric shelter, open pavilion or isolated tree cannot provide comparable protection.
Wait at least 30 minutes after the last thunder before returning outside. Reassess other hazards before departure.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Distinguish weather cover from lightning protection.
applies: Thunder is heard or a thunderstorm threat makes continued exposure unsafe.
equipment: Forecast, alert source and preidentified shelter destinations when available.

verify.text: Confirm what the shelter actually is and when thunder was last heard.

stop.text: If safe shelter is unavailable, remaining outdoors is hazardous. Seek the safest accessible option and avoid treating any outdoor location as safe from lightning.

diagram: Hear thunder | Substantial shelter | Wait after last thunder
visual: Sequence identifies the shelter class and the condition for resuming outdoor activity.

title: Keep insulation dry across a stop

action.text: Adjust layers before heavy exertion and use ventilation where weather permits. Avoid getting clothing wet with sweat.
Before a stop, find wind protection and add the reserved dry layer. Separate wet items from dry insulation.
Check companions for unusual fumbles, slurred speech or confusion as exposure continues.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Prevent sweat, wet gear and precipitation from soaking rest layers.
applies: Cold travel where activity alternates with standing or resting.
equipment: Dry spare insulation, weather shell and pack protection for dry items.

verify.text: The rest layer is dry and easy to reach, and the group can stop without standing in exposed wind.

stop.text: Suspected hypothermia needs medical help and protection against further cooling.

diagram: Vent during effort | Add dry insulation at rest | Check the group
visual: The dry reserve is used at the activity-to-rest transition.

title: Put a campfire completely out
origin: Smokey Bear campfire guide; new manuscript

action.text: Add water until active burning stops. Stir ash and embers to expose hot material.
Add more water as needed and check for remaining heat. Allow the material to cool completely before departing.
Keep someone at the site until the final check passes. Coal can remain hot after visible flame disappears.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Detect and eliminate hot material before anyone leaves a campfire.
applies: A small attended campfire in an authorized ring or site. A spreading fire is a different emergency.
equipment: Water and a stirring tool.

verify.text: No heat remains when checked safely without touching suspected embers.

stop.text: If a fire escapes your control, move to safety and call emergency services.

diagram: Drown burning material | Stir to expose hot spots | Cool completely
visual: A repeated water-and-stir cycle ends only at the cool condition.

title: Separate camp fuel from enclosed shelter
origin: B012 P14/P18 and CPSC camping equipment

action.text: Keep fuel-burning camping equipment out of tents, vehicles and other enclosed sleeping spaces. Arrange the cooking area outdoors and follow equipment clearances.
Use dry layers and ground insulation for warmth in sleeping areas. Keep the exit clear.
If CO exposure is suspected, move to fresh air immediately and call emergency services.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Prevent exposure from using fuel appliances in a tent or vehicle.
applies: Fuel-burning stoves, heaters, charcoal and similar camping appliances.
equipment: Product instructions, a lawful outdoor location and non-combustion alternatives for warmth.

verify.text: The appliance is outside and exhaust cannot enter the occupied shelter.

stop.text: Headache, dizziness, nausea or confusion during fuel use warrants immediate action.

diagram: Fuel and exhaust outside | Enclosed shelter separate | Fresh air and help if exposed
visual: Appliance location and occupied enclosure appear as separate control points.
reviewer: Carbon monoxide safety and emergency medicine

title: Place a portable generator outdoors
origin: CPSC portable generator guidance; new manuscript

action.text: Locate a suitable outdoor position at least 20 feet from the home. Direct exhaust away from the home and other occupied buildings.
Keep the generator out of the garage, porch enclosure and other occupied or partially enclosed spaces. Follow the manufacturer and a qualified electrician for connection requirements.
If CO is suspected, get to fresh air immediately and call emergency services.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Plan generator placement that keeps exhaust away from the occupied building.
applies: Household portable fuel-powered generator during a power outage.
equipment: Generator instructions, outdoor location and working CO alarms appropriate to the home.

verify.text: Check the path from the outlet to doors, windows and vents. Reassess if the location or direction changes.

stop.text: If you cannot provide the outdoor location and separation, leave the generator off.

diagram: Generator outdoors | At least 20 feet from home | Exhaust directed away
visual: Not-to-scale placement decision. The numeric clearance applies to portable generators.

title: Prepare water before starting
origin: B008 and Smokey Bear campfire guide

action.text: Put extinguishing water and tool within reach outside the hot area. Assign an attendant who will stay until the site is cold.
Keep combustible supplies away from the ring and establish where the group will stand or walk.
Stop before ignition if the water is lost, frozen or insufficient. Choose the no-fire plan rather than relying on a distant source.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Prevent an ignition attempt from starting before extinguishing resources are in place.
applies: A lawful outdoor fire where weather, site and attendance have already been checked.
equipment: Ready water, stirring tool, ring and accessible non-fire alternative.

verify.text: The attendant can locate water and tool without crossing the fire area.

stop.text: Changing conditions or a loss of equipment triggers a fresh authorization and site check.

diagram: Place water and tool | Assign an attendant | Light only after checks
visual: Extinguishing equipment precedes ignition.

title: Reject a contaminated source

action.text: Identify available safe water first. Check where runoff comes from and whether a local warning applies.
Reject sources suspected of fuel, toxic chemicals or radioactive contamination. Seek a known safe source and follow local instructions.
If only microbial contamination is suspected, select an appropriate microbial treatment and protect clean storage.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Screen for chemical contamination before choosing microbial treatment.
applies: Selecting a water source after a spill, flood or uncertain local advisory.
equipment: Known potable alternative and local advisory if available.

verify.text: State which hazard the procedure handles and which hazards required rejecting the source.

stop.text: Clear appearance, lack of odor or successful boiling cannot override a suspected chemical hazard.

diagram: Identify supply | Reject chemical hazards | Treat remaining microbial risk
visual: Source rejection is a decision upstream of all treatment.

title: Boil for microbial treatment

action.text: Settle cloudy water or strain it through clean cloth before boiling. Use a stable setup according to equipment instructions.
Bring the water to a rolling boil and keep it there one minute. Above 6,500 feet, maintain the boil for three minutes.
Cool the water and keep it covered in a clean sanitized container. Use clean tools to avoid recontamination.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Apply the correct boiling endpoint and separate it from preclarification.
applies: Water with an acceptable chemical source history and suspected microbial contamination. Stable safe heat is available.
equipment: Clean heat-safe pot, safe heat source, timer or watch and sanitized covered container.

verify.text: Start timing only after a rolling boil begins, and protect the finished batch from raw water.

stop.text: Use an alternate supply if chemical contamination is suspected or the pot or heat source is unsafe.

diagram: Clarify if cloudy | Rolling boil plus timer | Cool and cover
visual: Boiling is the microbial treatment step. Clarification and storage are separate.

title: Pair filtration with disinfection
origin: B009 revision and CDC backcountry guide

action.text: Check product labels, intended organisms and operating conditions. Typical portable filters leave gaps, especially for viruses.
Filter and then disinfect according to each product's directions, including concentration, contact time and water conditions.
Keep any part that contacted raw water from the clean outlet and storage vessel.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Choose a matched backcountry treatment sequence and identify its limits.
applies: An acceptable chemical source and documented equipment capable of addressing expected microbes.
equipment: Matched filter and disinfectant with readable instructions; clean container.

verify.text: Name each product, target limitation and the actual contact time used before drinking.

stop.text: Do not improvise a dose or assume an unknown filter covers viruses or chemicals. Use another known-safe supply or a supported procedure.

diagram: Check what filter covers | Disinfect as directed | Protect clean side
visual: Devices are separate barriers with different contaminant limits.

title: Keep treated water clean

action.text: Use a suitable vessel with known previous use. Reject one that held toxic chemicals.
Mark raw and finished containers. Keep the lid, threads and outlet on the clean side of the workflow.
Dispense without introducing unclean hands, cups or raw-water implements. Close the vessel after use.

technical_review: AI editorial check; qualified reviewer pending
objective: Store drinking water without mixing it with raw sources or contaminated utensils.
applies: Treated or commercially potable water kept for later use.
equipment: Clean, sanitized tight-closing food-grade containers and separate raw-water container.

verify.text: Containers stay distinguishable and the storage cap and dispensing surfaces remain clean.

stop.text: If untreated water or suspect contact mixes with finished water, withhold it until an appropriate treatment decision is made. Suspected chemical contamination requires another supply.

diagram: Raw side separate | Clean closed vessel | Clean dispensing
visual: Physical separation reduces accidental transfer at the container opening.
